metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

evidence.quote: Only contribute code that you fully understand. See also our [AI policy][llm].
If you use LLM / "AI" tools for your contributions, please read and follow our [_Generative AI / LLM Policy_][llm].

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for AI-assisted code
domains.reasoning: CONTRIBUTING.md names code contributions and AI tool use, and states a requirement (contributor must fully understand the code, implying human oversight/human_in_the_loop) but the substance of any concrete supervision rule is deferred to an external 'AI policy' document not in scope. Within this file itself, no accountability holder (e.g. 'contributor is responsible') is stated, only an obligation ('only contribute code you fully understand'), so accountability stays not_specified. Scored partial: area is named, supervision partially implied, but accountability and scope are left open within this file.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots at all
domains.reasoning: The file contains no reference to meetings, recordings, or notetaker/meeting bots of any kind.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule for AI use in docs/content authoring
domains.reasoning: There is a detailed Documentation section (style, docstrings, semantic newlines) but nothing in it addresses AI-generated or AI-assisted documentation, blog posts, or design assets.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use in moderation actions
domains.reasoning: No text discusses moderation decisions (e.g. banning, closing issues, enforcement) being made or assisted by AI.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI-assisted review of contributions
domains.reasoning: The Governance section states 'everyone is welcome to review/merge pull requests of others but nobody is allowed to merge their own code', but this concerns human review rights/self-merge restrictions, not AI use in reviewing. No mention of AI tools being used to review PRs.
No mention of autonomous agents or bots acting on the repository without human oversight.

The phrase 'Don't waste energy / tokens on something that we do not want' is about avoiding wasted human/contributor effort on unwanted large PRs before discussion, not a statement about the environmental (energy/water/carbon) footprint of AI tooling. No rule or rationale about environmental impact is present.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on server load or hardware cost
domains.reasoning: No text discusses server load, CI infrastructure cost, or hardware financing in relation to AI use. The CI/tox discussion is unrelated to AI.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on project data being used to train models
domains.reasoning: No mention of the project's issues, discussions, code, or user data being used (or protected from being used) to train AI models.

unscoped_statements.quote: If you use LLM / "AI" tools for your contributions, please read and follow our [_Generative AI / LLM Policy_][llm].

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: CONTRIBUTING.md itself sets almost no AI-specific rules; it briefly touches code contributions (requiring contributors to fully understand any code they submit and pointing to an external, out-of-scope AI/LLM policy for the substance), while notetaker bots, content, moderation, review, autonomous use, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and training data are entirely unaddressed within this file.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
